## Story-level uncertainties

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj  (`#the-barrier`)

Cited ayat: 18:94-98

> **18:94** قَالُوا۟ يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا
>
> **18:95** قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌ فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا
>
> **18:96** ءَاتُونِى زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُوا۟ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُۥ نَارًا قَالَ ءَاتُونِىٓ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا
>
> **18:97** فَمَا ٱسْطَٰعُوٓا۟ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ لَهُۥ نَقْبًا
>
> **18:98** قَالَ هَٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّى فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى جَعَلَهُۥ دَكَّآءَ وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى حَقًّا

### Claims

**c1** (18:94): They told Dhul-Qarnayn that Ya'juj and Ma'juj were causing corruption in the land.

**c2** (18:94): They asked whether they might pay him a charge on condition that he set a barrier between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj.

**c3** (18:95): Dhul-Qarnayn said that what his Lord had established him in was better, and told them to help him with strength so that he might make a rampart between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj.

**c4** (18:96): He told them to bring him sheets of iron, and when he had made it level between the cliffs he told them to blow, and when he had made it fire he told them to bring him molten copper to pour over it.

**c5** (18:97): Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb over it, and could not pierce it.

**c6** (18:98): Dhul-Qarnayn said that this was a mercy from his Lord, that when the promise of his Lord came He would make it level, and that the promise of his Lord is true.

### One-minute summary

The people told Dhul-Qarnayn that Ya'juj and Ma'juj caused corruption in the land and asked for a barrier [c1][c2]. He built a rampart of iron and copper, and Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb it or pierce it [c4][c5].

### Complete story

They told Dhul-Qarnayn that Ya'juj and Ma'juj were causing corruption in the land [c1]. They asked whether they might pay him a charge on condition that he set a barrier between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj [c2]. Dhul-Qarnayn said that what his Lord had established him in was better, and told them to help him with strength so that he might make a rampart between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj [c3]. He told them to bring him sheets of iron, and when he had made it level between the cliffs he told them to blow, and when he had made it fire he told them to bring him molten copper to pour over it [c4]. Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb over it, and could not pierce it [c5]. Dhul-Qarnayn said that this was a mercy from his Lord, that when the promise of his Lord came He would make it level, and that the promise of his Lord is true [c6].

### Deep study

- They told Dhul-Qarnayn that Ya'juj and Ma'juj were causing corruption in the land (18:94) [c1].
- They asked whether they might pay him a charge on condition that he set a barrier between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj (18:94) [c2].
- Dhul-Qarnayn said that what his Lord had established him in was better, and told them to help him with strength so that he might make a rampart between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj (18:95) [c3].
- He told them to bring him sheets of iron, and when he had made it level between the cliffs he told them to blow, and when he had made it fire he told them to bring him molten copper to pour over it (18:96) [c4].
- Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb over it, and could not pierce it (18:97) [c5].
- Dhul-Qarnayn said that this was a mercy from his Lord, that when the promise of his Lord came He would make it level, and that the promise of his Lord is true (18:98) [c6].

### Kids mode

The people asked Dhul-Qarnayn to build a barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj [c2]. He used iron and copper [c4]. Ya'juj and Ma'juj could not climb it or pierce it [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Dhul-Qarnayn answers the offer of payment by saying that what his Lord has established him in is better, and asks only for help [c3]. One reading is that he describes the finished barrier as a mercy from his Lord and refers its end to his Lord's promise [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who Ya'juj and Ma'juj are, where they live or where the barrier stands; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: who the people who spoke to Dhul-Qarnayn were; the ayah does not name them.
- Not established: the Arabic of 18:96 speaks of the cliffs in a dual form; the draft renders it as the cliffs.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of Ya'juj and Ma'juj with Gog and Magog or with a particular people, and any place for the barrier; none is used here.

## 2. When they are let loose  (`#when-they-are-let-loose`)

Cited ayat: 18:99, 21:96-97

> **18:99** وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِى بَعْضٍ وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَٰهُمْ جَمْعًا

> **21:96** حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ
>
> **21:97** وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (18:99): The Quran says that on that day God will leave some of them surging over others, and that the horn will be blown and God will gather them all together.

**c2** (21:96): It says that Ya'juj and Ma'juj will be let loose and will descend from every high place.

**c3** (21:97): It says that the true promise will draw near and the gaze of those who disbelieved will be fixed.

**c4** (21:97): They will say that they had been heedless of this, and that they were wrongdoers.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that Ya'juj and Ma'juj will be let loose and descend from every high place [c2]. It says that the true promise will draw near and that those who disbelieved will say they had been heedless [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The Quran says that on that day God will leave some of them surging over others, and that the horn will be blown and God will gather them all together [c1]. It says that Ya'juj and Ma'juj will be let loose and will descend from every high place [c2]. It says that the true promise will draw near and the gaze of those who disbelieved will be fixed [c3]. They will say that they had been heedless of this, and that they were wrongdoers [c4].

### Deep study

- The Quran says that on that day God will leave some of them surging over others, and that the horn will be blown and God will gather them all together (18:99) [c1].
- It says that Ya'juj and Ma'juj will be let loose and will descend from every high place (21:96) [c2].
- It says that the true promise will draw near and the gaze of those who disbelieved will be fixed (21:97) [c3].
- They will say that they had been heedless of this, and that they were wrongdoers (21:97) [c4].

### Kids mode

The Quran says that one day Ya'juj and Ma'juj will be let loose [c2]. Those who did not believe will say that they had not paid attention [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage joins the release of Ya'juj and Ma'juj with the nearing of the true promise [c2][c3]. One reading is that the words of those who disbelieved ask the hearer not to be heedless [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who is meant by some of them in 18:99 (Ya'juj and Ma'juj, or the people gathered on that day); the ayah does not say.
- Not established: when the release will happen or how it relates to the barrier of 18:98; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the ayat of 21:96 do not name the place from which they descend.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: reports about the signs of the Hour that name Ya'juj and Ma'juj; none is used here.
